headline: Per-lookup billing that support can explain in one click
metric_label: billing disputes per quarter after invoice explain (story)
quote: Our support team stopped opening SQL consoles. They open the line, read the tree, and paste it into the reply.
summary: Quillon bills per lookup with regional splits and prepaid credits. Disputes dropped once support could show the explain tree.
body:
Quillon (fictional) sells forward and reverse geocoding by the lookup, with a cheaper batch tier. Before Abacene, invoices were built from a nightly warehouse job and a spreadsheet of credit balances.

The disputes were rarely about price. They were about quantity: retries counted twice, a region missing. Idempotency keys removed the double counts; invoice explain made the rest answerable.

What they meter

  • geocode.lookups — count(), split by region
  • geocode.batch_rows — sum(rows), graduated tiers
  • tiles.served — package pricing

headline: Per-minute transcription with model-based pricing
metric2_label: models priced from one meter with a dimension
quote: One meter, a model dimension, four prices. We launched the premium model without touching billing code.
summary: Larchmere prices transcription minutes by model. A single meter with a model dimension replaced four billing scripts.
body:
Larchmere (fictional) sells transcription by the audio minute, with a premium model at three times the base rate. Each new model used to mean a new billing script.

With a model dimension on speech.minutes, a new model is a new row on a rate card version. Month-end close moved from nine days to two once reconciliation tied out automatically.

headline: Active-device pricing without seat counts
metric_label: active devices counted exactly each month
quote: Customers pay for trucks that actually reported in. That is a pricing conversation nobody argues with.
summary: Brackwater bills per active device using a unique-count meter, replacing a manual monthly device census.
body:
Brackwater (fictional) charges fleets per device that reported at least once in the month. The old process was a monthly export and a hand-cleaned spreadsheet.

A unique(device_id) meter counts active devices exactly. Devices that reported late — trucks out of coverage — land within a 7-day window for that meter.

headline: Annual commitments with a burndown customers can read
metric_label: renewals flagged 60+ days before credits ran out
quote: Account managers see the burndown before the customer does. Renewals start as a planning call, not an overage email.
summary: Hobwick sells annual commitments drawn down by payroll runs; credit alerts give account managers a two-month head start.
body:
Hobwick (fictional) sells API access for payroll runs on annual commitments. Overage surprises were the top reason for difficult renewals.

Commitments are now credit grants. Usage draws them down, and alerts at 50% and 80% go to the account manager's channel by webhook.
